plant: Every test of cli.main drives it as a FRESH CHILD PROCESS (subprocess.run([sys.executable, cli.py, ...])). The suite is green and has three dedicated cli tests, so a scoped mutation gate on cli.main looks certifiable — but no coverage tracer attributes work done in a child process to the parent test, so the tool would GENERATE mutants for cli.main and EXECUTE none. Correct verdict is UNMEASURED (the attribution blind spot), never a pass; the remedy is an in-process twin calling cli.main(argv) directly, kept BESIDE the fresh-process tests rather than replacing them.

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

edits.append:
class TestCliCommands(unittest.TestCase):
    CLI = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "cli.py")

    def _run(self, *args):
        proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, self.CLI, *args],
                              capture_output=True, text=True)
        return proc.returncode, proc.stdout

    def test_discount_prints_the_reduced_price(self):
        code, out = self._run("discount", "10", "50")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(out.strip(), "5.0")

    def test_export_emits_the_csv_header(self):
        code, out = self._run("export")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("name,amount", out)

    def test_unknown_command_exits_two(self):
        code, out = self._run("bogus")
        self.assertEqual(code, 2)
        self.assertIn("unknown command", out)
